[Hacker News — openai.com]
(opens in a new window) GPT-6.2 Sol: our go-to model for everyday work GPT-6.2 Sol: our go-to model for everyday work Professional outputs that match industry standards Computer use and interactive web design Efficient workflows with cleaner code style Cybersecurity capabilities Safety and alignment Pricing and availability GPT-6.2 Sol: our go-to model for everyday work Professional outputs that match industry standards Computer use and interactive web design Efficient workflows with cleaner code style Cybersecurity capabilities Safety and alignment Pricing and availability We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra , our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol , our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. For businesses and developers, that means frontier performance at costs that make sense at scale.

GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new quality bar for AI in complex professional work. Its slides, spreadsheets, and documents read less like AI, and more closely follow the templates you provide and the conventions of your field. It writes cleaner code and builds frontends that look and work better, particularly for websites, gaming, and 3D design.

On Agents’ Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT‑6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.

Agents’ Last Exam evaluates models on long-horizon professional workflows. Its leaderboard results for Fable 5.2 exclude nine tasks that used a fallback model.

We believe GPT-6.2 Astra is the best model in the world for scientists. It sets a new high on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which tests how well models can carry out scientific work in a terminal. GPT-6.2 Astra scores 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than one-third the cost. It also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index, which asks models to interpret real biological data and run experiments to infer how a simulated system works.

In the API, GPT‑6.2 Astra’s input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT‑6 Astra’s, with a 60% discount on cached input ($8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output, all per million tokens). GPT‑6.2 Sol keeps GPT‑6.1 Sol’s API token prices. On several benchmarks, both models come close to or outperform other leading models at a small fraction of the cost per task.

Compared with GPT‑6.1 Sol, GPT‑6.2 Sol is smarter, more efficient, and lets you complete more tasks on the same paid plan. It powers through multistep agentic workflows, writes clearly and naturally, and is intuitive to collaborate with. Many employees at OpenAI use it as their default model for both technical and non-technical tasks.

In Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0, GPT‑6.2 Sol comes within 0.5 points of GPT‑6.2 Astra at about one-fifth the cost (both at max).

FrontierCode 2.0 evaluates whether changes to real codebases meet maintainers’ standards for merging.

Its speed and intelligence also make it ideal for the important tasks people turn to AI for outside of work. On our recently released LifeVal ⁠ evaluation, which measures performance on challenging everyday tasks, GPT‑6.2 Sol outscores GPT‑6 Astra at about one-seventh the cost.

LifeVal tests how well models handle everyday tasks tailored to someone’s needs, such as shortlisting kindergartens after a move, finding a home that fits a family’s budget and commute, or planning meals for a parent adjusting to a new diagnosis.

We trained GPT‑6.2 Astra to create clearer, better-designed slides, spreadsheets, and documents that more closely follow the conventions professionals use in fields like law, sales, finance, and accounting. The writing is more direct and specific, with fewer generic takeaways and less filler.

Harvey LAB‑AA v1.1 uses legal assignments to test whether models can find the relevant facts across source documents, apply them to a detailed brief, and produce an accurate deliverable that meets every requirement. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new state of the art, more than doubling Claude Fable 5.2’s pass rate at about one-sixth the cost. Astra for Law ⁠ , our configuration of GPT-6.2 Astra for lawyers, scores even higher on this benchmark.

Harvey LAB‑AA tests legal work such as reviewing contract provisions. Its headline score gives credit only when a deliverable meets every grading criterion and contains no material hallucinations.

Our internal GDPval v2 benchmark is our next iteration of GDPval ⁠ that measures complex, long-horizon workflows from real projects in sectors like consulting, finance, and design. GPT‑6.2 Astra leads the models we tested, up 6.2 percentage points from GPT‑6 Astra while using 22% fewer output tokens. GPT‑6.2 Sol improves 5.3 points from GPT‑6.1 Sol.

GDPval v2 consists of long-horizon knowledge-work assignments from r

[Simon Willison — simonwillison.net]
We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work.

They're available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . I shipped LLM 0.38 with support for the new models.

6.2 Astra is 80% of the price of 6 Astra - $8/MTok input and $40/MTok output, the same price as Claude Fable 5.2 (which was also 80% of its predecessor). 6 Astra and Fable 5 were both $10/$50. The cached price is an even bigger discount - $0.40/million compared to $1/million for the older model. This is great news for longer running agentic sessions.

GPT-6.2 Sol is the same $2/$10 price as 6.1 Sol and 6 Sol - which are half the price of GPT-5.6 Sol ($4/$20).

Here are the pelicans for GPT-6.2 Sol and for GPT-6.2 Astra . The 6.2 Astra max pelican looks like this:

I have a full comparison grid here , but here's how the high/xhigh/max pelicans compare with the previous Sol and Astra releases:

I also ran my most recent benchmark prompt against the two models, using "Ultra' effort levels in the Codex CLI:

Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data

Here's Sol and here's Astra . Neither of them did a good enough job of morphing Yonkers into a big mech, at least in comparison to Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon .

This video showing the Astra and Sol animations playing out at the same time:

I created that video using GPT-6.2 Astra (Ultra) in the Codex desktop app by prompting:

https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-astra-ultra/index.html and https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-sol-ultra/index.html are two videos of the same thing by two different models

I need a video of the first 10 seconds where the top half of the video plays the first and the bottom half plays the second

I need an overlaid label of "GPT-6.2 Astra" on the top half and "GPT-6.2 Sol" on the bottom half. These labels should be tastefully positioned.

The buzz around these new models is mixed at the moment. Astra 6.2 isn't scoring quite as high as Fable 5.2 on various benchmarks, and I've seen a few complaints that its communication style can be confusing. Theo Browne's review (in the form of a feedback letter he sent OpenAI during pre-release) has this useful example:

When this model is working on long tasks, it can pull in a lot of subagents and manage them pretty well. It will then proceed to randomly ask you some weird internal implementation detail bullshit that you could not under any earthly circumstance understand, much less have input on .

I sent "/goal make a new level for Outer Wilds". 2 hours in, it's "blocked" because it wanted to ask me "does r24's reviewer write it's clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4?"

This is a link post by Simon Willison, posted on 17th November 2026 .

reactions: [Hacker News] Haiku 5.6 is a surprisingly good model (and IME better than Luna), but the price jump at 100k context and the short TTL of Anthropic caches makes it a less interesting choice interactive use cases where Luna suffices. It is most likely meant for subagents. Also, for long contexts, Haiku 5.5's direct competitor is probably Terra 6.1; similar cost per task with longer cache TTL and equal or bet
[Hacker News] Yes, folks need to remember what powers Microsoft Copilot.
[Hacker News] Inference has been ~80-90% margin. It’s more showing how overpriced API pricing has been all along.

[Hacker News] What? Just today I forgot to tell Opus 5.5 where the source code repository is in a multi-repo setup, and Opus 5.5 proactively disassembled the binary to figure out what the code does. I didn’t even intend to have it do binary reverse engineering and yet it did that.

[Hacker News] I run an internal OCR benchmark for historical research (old texts.. newspapers, typewriter, but also handwritten) Google is BY FAR at the top of the Pareto frontier, perhaps b/c of Google Books. But Sol 6.2 (low) is the first non-Google model that grazes that frontier. Sure, it's still more expensive than Hydrogen, but not too far! (and that's at the current low Hydrogen prices)

[Hacker News] From the reactions I've been seeing it seems like they're atrocious, absolutely terrible. People who've been using it, what do you think? Is it actually that bad? Surely it has strengths right?
